meta.note: Strategy lab specification. Everything here is a DESIGN, not a result. No strategy on this page has been backtested, because no historical odds archive has been ingested (Q-011). Any cell that would contain a measured result is blank and flagged.

status_meaning.Proposed: Described but never tested. No claim of profitability is made.
status_meaning.Not started: Identified as needed, not yet designed.

pipeline.name: Ingest
pipeline.detail: Pull every Tier 1 and Tier 2 input and stamp it with the exact retrieval time. Never impute a missing value.
pipeline.note: Week 10 injury report and 2026 standings ingested. No odds feed, no transactions feed, no schedule.

pipeline.name: Normalise
pipeline.detail: Map every input to a stable identifier (game, team, player, position group) so that a player who changes team is still the same player.
pipeline.note: Blocked until an official player identifier source is confirmed.

pipeline.name: Feature
pipeline.detail: Turn normalised inputs into the signal values listed in the signal catalogue.
pipeline.note: Depends on step 2 and on the depth inference (S-007).

pipeline.name: Model
pipeline.detail: Produce a probability for each market outcome, not a pick.
pipeline.note: Model class not chosen; choosing it before having data would be guesswork.

pipeline.name: Calibrate
pipeline.detail: Check that outcomes called 60% actually happen 60% of the time. Recalibrate on a held-out window.

pipeline.name: De-vig
pipeline.detail: Strip the book's margin from the market price before any comparison. Record which method was used.
pipeline.note: See suggestion S-003. Default: proportional; sensitivity check: Shin.

pipeline.name: Price
pipeline.detail: Convert the model probability to a fair price in the market's own format. This is the 'own line' the brief asks for.
pipeline.note: Fair price conversion is pure arithmetic from the model probability.

pipeline.name: Compare
pipeline.detail: Edge exists only where the de-vigged market price is worse than our fair price by more than the cost hurdle.
pipeline.note: Cost hurdle anchored to Nevada sports pool hold, 6.06% fiscal-year-to-date (SRC-007).

pipeline.name: Gate
pipeline.detail: Run gates G0 to G5 in order. Fail means return to research, not a waiver.

pipeline.name: Size
pipeline.detail: Fractional Kelly, one quarter, capped at 1% of bankroll per position (S-013), until the owner sets otherwise.

pipeline.name: Log
pipeline.detail: Record the bet, the price captured at placement, the model probability and the strategy version, all at placement time.
pipeline.note: This is what makes CLV measurable. Build it before the first bet, not after.

pipeline.name: Score
pipeline.detail: Capture the closing price, compute CLV, and grade against the gates - not against whether the bet won.
pipeline.note: Depends on step 11 and on an odds archive.

formulas.name: Implied probability from American odds
formulas.formula: positive odds: p = 100 / (odds + 100)   |   negative odds: p = |odds| / (|odds| + 100)

formulas.name: Proportional de-vig
formulas.note: One of at least four competing methods. Which best recovers realised frequency is untested here - see S-003.

formulas.name: Fair American odds from a probability
Closing Line Value
formulas.formula: CLV = p_close_our_side - p_taken_our_side, using de-vigged probabilities on both sides
formulas.note: Positive CLV means we took a better price than the market closed at. It does not by itself prove the bet was good.

formulas.name: Fractional Kelly stake
formulas.formula: f* = k * (b*p - q) / b, where b = decimal odds - 1, q = 1 - p, k = fraction (proposed 0.25)
formulas.note: Full Kelly (k=1) is deliberately rejected: it maximises growth only if p is exact, and p never is.

formulas.name: Breakeven win rate at a given price
formulas.formula: breakeven = p_implied_de_vigged ; a strategy must beat this, not 50%
formulas.note: The most common error in betting analysis is comparing a win rate to 50% instead of to the price-implied breakeven.

signals.name: Practice-participation delta
signals.hypothesis: A player who deteriorates across the three practice days is more likely to be unavailable than a single day's status implies, and the market under-reacts to the trajectory rather than the level.
signals.note: The official report shows only the current day's status on the page surface; the day-by-day history must be captured as it is filed, or it is lost.

signals.name: Offensive line continuity
signals.hypothesis: The count of offensive linemen not participating is more predictive of offensive output than any single named player's status.
signals.note: Directly testable today: the Week 10 report gives position for every listed player.

signals.name: Secondary depletion
signals.hypothesis: A defence missing multiple defensive backs concedes more explosive passes than the standings-based expectation implies.
signals.inputs: Official injury report, position filter (SRC-001); standings pass defence proxy (SRC-002)
signals.note: Blocked on the depth-inference work (S-007) for the 2nd/3rd/4th string weighting.

signals.name: Pass-rush availability
signals.hypothesis: Edge defender availability shifts pressure rate, which shifts the opposing quarterback's efficiency more than the spread accounts for.

signals.name: Confirmed quarterback change
signals.hypothesis: A confirmed change of starting quarterback is the single largest lineup-driven repricing event, and the market moves on the announcement rather than on the underlying quality gap.
signals.inputs: Official NFL.com news (SRC-003) and official transactions (SRC-011)
signals.note: Demonstrably necessary: the Seahawks case (F-004) shows this information never appears in the injury report.

signals.name: Backfield depth stress
signals.hypothesis: When the top two running backs on a team are both limited or worse, the offence shifts pass-heavy in a way the market prices late.
signals.note: Requires the depth inference to know who the 'top two' are.

signals.name: Rest and bye differential
signals.hypothesis: A team coming off a bye against one that is not, and teams on equal rest, differ in second-half performance.
signals.note: Blocked: bye weeks are currently only inferred (F-008) and the schedule has not been ingested.

signals.name: Travel and time-zone shift
signals.hypothesis: West coast teams travelling east for an early kickoff underperform their own baseline.
signals.note: Blocked: home/away is not currently asserted (F-009).

signals.name: Pace and neutral-situation rate
signals.hypothesis: Teams that run plays faster than the market's implied pace generate more total plays, which lifts both team totals and volume-based player props.

signals.name: Red-zone efficiency regression
signals.hypothesis: Red-zone touchdown rate is noisy and mean-reverting; teams running hot convert fewer field goals, which is mispriced in team totals and kicker props.

signals.name: Turnover regression
signals.hypothesis: Takeaway rate is the least repeatable team statistic in football; teams riding an extreme takeaway rate are mispriced in the spread.

signals.name: Weather effect on totals and kicking
signals.hypothesis: Wind above a threshold and precipitation depress passing volume and kicking accuracy more than the total accounts for.
signals.inputs: NOAA / National Weather Service (SRC-008); official venue and surface data
signals.note: Blocked: no weather data ingested, and venue dome status is unverified.

signals.name: Divisional familiarity
signals.hypothesis: Divisional games are lower scoring and more likely to be decided by a field goal than the market's generic spread implies.
signals.note: Partially unblocked: divisions are verified from official standings; schedule is not.

signals.name: Lookahead and sandwich spots
signals.hypothesis: A team with a high-profile game next week underperforms in the present week.

signals.name: Points-versus-wins divergence
signals.hypothesis: A team whose win record outruns its scoring margin is overpriced; the reverse is underpriced.
signals.note: Fully unblocked: PF and PA are verified official values for all 32 teams.

signals.name: Primetime overreaction
signals.hypothesis: The public over-reacts to a primetime blowout, and the following week's line for that team is biased.
signals.inputs: Official results; market prices (no official source - F-002)

signals.name: Target share versus prop line
signals.hypothesis: A receiver whose target share exceeds what his receiving-yard prop implies is underpriced, controlling for the game total.
signals.inputs: Official play-by-play (source to be confirmed); market prop lines (no official source)

signals.name: Correlated same-game combination
signals.hypothesis: Legitimately correlated legs are underpriced by naive multiplication, but only where the correlation has actually been estimated.
signals.inputs: Correlation register; market prop lines (no official source)
signals.note: Explicitly blocked until correlations are estimated - see F-010. This signal must not be used before then.

gates.name: Data integrity
gates.question: Can every input be traced to a Tier 1 or Tier 2 source, and was any missing value imputed?
gates.threshold: Zero imputed values. Every input carries a source id and a retrieval timestamp.
gates.on_fail: Return to research. Imputation is not permitted.

gates.name: Pre-registration
gates.question: Was the hypothesis written down before the results were looked at?
gates.threshold: Hypothesis, bet universe, price source and bet-timing rule all fixed and timestamped before scoring.
gates.on_fail: Return to research. A hypothesis formed after seeing results is a story, not a strategy.

gates.name: Sample size
gates.question: Is there enough data for luck to be a plausible explanation of nothing?
gates.threshold: PROPOSED: at least 1,000 graded bets, spanning at least 2 seasons and at least 200 distinct games.
gates.on_fail: Return to research. Threshold is a proposal awaiting ratification - it is a design choice, not a measured fact.

gates.name: Economic hurdle
gates.question: Does the estimated edge clear the cost of doing business?
gates.threshold: Estimated edge after de-vig must exceed the cost hurdle. Reference hurdle: Nevada sports pool hold, 6.06% fiscal-year-to-date (SRC-007).
gates.on_fail: Return to research. An edge smaller than the margin is not an edge.

gates.name: Out-of-sample
gates.question: Does it survive data it was not built on?
gates.threshold: On a frozen, single-use holdout: mean CLV above zero, and realised return no worse than the negative of the cost hurdle.
gates.on_fail: Return to research. In-sample performance is not evidence.

gates.name: Luck separation
gates.question: Could a random bettor have produced this?
gates.threshold: Three independent checks must all pass: binomial test of the win rate against the price-implied breakeven; bootstrap 95% confidence interval on mean CLV excluding zero; Monte Carlo comparison against a random bettor placing the same number of bets at the same price distribution, p below 0.05.
gates.on_fail: Return to research. Failing any one of the three is failing the gate.

leaderboard.reported_not_scored: Realised profit and loss, sample size, longest drawdown
leaderboard.rationale: Profit is not a skill measure over any sample we can realistically obtain. CLV is observable immediately after each bet and is not contaminated by result variance. Calibration is used as a tiebreak so that a strategy cannot win by simply agreeing with the market on easy games.
leaderboard.minimum_bets_floor: PROPOSED: 500 graded bets before a strategy appears on the board at all.
anti_gaming_rules: Strategy versions are immutable once registered (S-010).
The holdout window is scored once and never re-tuned afterwards.
Every bet is logged at placement time with the price captured at that moment.
All strategies are corrected for multiple comparisons across the board, because a leaderboard of many strategies guarantees some will look good by chance.
Sequential peeking is not permitted: a strategy cannot be declared skilful the moment it crosses a threshold. Evaluation points are fixed in advance.

proposed: Tier 1 - Top CLV, minimum bets met: promoted to live staking with the largest allocation.
Tier 2 - Positive CLV with a confidence interval excluding zero: promoted to live staking with a reduced allocation.
Tier 3 - Passes G0-G4 but not G5: stays in research, no allocation.
Fail - Any gate failed: returned to research.
rewards.note: Rewards are deliberately tied to the gates, not to profit, so that the incentive is to find skill rather than to find variance.

skill_vs_luck.principle: Luck is removed by measuring the decision, not the outcome. A bet can be correct and lose. The only measurable evidence of skill available before a long results sample exists is whether the bettor consistently obtained a better price than the market's final price.

methods.name: Closing Line Value
methods.detail: Compare the de-vigged probability of the price taken against the de-vigged probability of the closing price. Available immediately; not contaminated by result variance.
methods.limitation: Rewards agreement with the closing market. If the closing market is systematically wrong, CLV will not detect it.

methods.name: Binomial test against price-implied breakeven
methods.detail: Test the win rate against the breakeven implied by the prices taken, not against 50%.
methods.limitation: Low power at realistic sample sizes; a genuinely skilled bettor can fail this test for seasons.

methods.name: Bootstrap confidence interval on mean CLV
methods.detail: Resample the bet record to get a confidence interval that makes no distributional assumption about CLV.
methods.limitation: A wide interval is the honest answer at small samples, and it should be published rather than hidden.

methods.name: Monte Carlo null model
methods.detail: Simulate a random bettor placing the same number of bets at the same price distribution, many times, and see how often the null beats the strategy.
methods.limitation: Only as good as the null; a null that ignores bet selection will overstate skill.

methods.name: Calibration and log loss
methods.detail: Check that outcomes predicted at p occur with frequency p. A strategy can beat the closing line and still be badly calibrated.
methods.limitation: Needs a large sample to distinguish.

methods.name: Multiple-comparisons correction
methods.detail: With many strategies on a leaderboard, some will show significant results by chance alone. Correct across the board.
methods.limitation: Reduces power; that is the correct trade.

methods.name: Sequential testing guard
methods.detail: Fix the evaluation points in advance. Declaring skill the moment a threshold is crossed invalidates the test.

skill_vs_luck.what_we_cannot_yet_do: Every method above needs a bet record, and a bet record needs an odds feed. None of them has been run. No strategy on this site has a measured result.
